title: AirTag found moving with you: what to do
caption:
AirTag found moving with you? Your phone warns you about trackers.
But turning off Bluetooth won't stop it. Apple and Google say what does.
Is your tracker alert on? Yes or no?
keywords: does turning off bluetooth stop airtag tracking
how to tell if someone is tracking me with an airtag
airtag found moving with you meaning
pinned_comment: Short version: turning off Bluetooth won't stop a tracker. Apple and Google both say the owner can still see its location, so the fix is to disable the tracker itself, if it's safe. If you feel unsafe, go to a safe public location and contact law enforcement first. Check yours: Tracking Notifications on iPhone, Unknown tracker alerts on Android. Is yours on? Yes or no?

pinned_backups.if: I got the alert but I can't find the tracker.
pinned_backups.reply: Apple says to look in "an item that you don't check often, like a jacket pocket, the outer compartment of a bag, or your vehicle." Tap the alert and play a sound. If you can't find it and feel unsafe, Apple and Google both say: go to a safe public location and contact law enforcement.

pinned_backups.if: Play Sound is grayed out. Does that mean I'm fine?
pinned_backups.reply: Not necessarily. Apple: "the item might not be with you anymore or it's within range of its owner. Or if it was with you overnight, its identifier might have changed."

Same answer. Google: if you "turn on Airplane Mode, your phone won't prevent the owner of the tracker or device from finding the location of the tracker." And on iPhone, Apple says that in Airplane Mode "you won't receive tracking notifications."

pinned_backups.if: Will the owner know I played the sound?
pinned_backups.reply: Google says: "You won't notify the owner if you play the sound." That's Google's page; Apple's page doesn't say either way.

pinned_backups.if: It went off when I was with my friend.
pinned_backups.reply: That happens. Google: "You may get these notifications if you borrow an item or if you're traveling with someone who has a tracker with them." Apple says alerts can come from "borrowed AirPods, or AirPods inadvertently left behind by a friend or family member."

pinned_backups.if: Should I just turn the tracker off?
pinned_backups.reply: Only if it's safe. Google: "keep it turned on if you're concerned that turning it off could be unsafe." Some trackers "may be factory reset" when turned off, and then "Law enforcement can't get additional information about these trackers". Apple says law enforcement can work with Apple and you might need to provide the item and its serial number.

youtube_description:
Your phone warns you about trackers. If your iPhone shows "AirTag Found Moving With You", or your Android phone sends an unknown tracker alert, a compatible tracker that isn't yours might be moving with you. It could be in something you borrowed, like a backpack.
But turning off Bluetooth won't stop it: Apple and Google both say the owner can still see the tracker's location. So tap the alert and play a sound to find it. If you feel unsafe, go to a safe public location and contact law enforcement. If it's safe, disable the tracker itself. Then check yours: Settings › Notifications › Tracking Notifications on iPhone, Settings › Safety & emergency › Unknown tracker alerts on Android 12 and up.

Apple: "If any AirTag, AirPods, Find My network accessory, or compatible Bluetooth location-tracking device is separated from its owner and seen moving with you over time, you're notified". The item "could be traveling with you, and the owner might be able to see its location." "It's possible that the AirTag or Find My network accessory might be attached to an item you're borrowing."

Apple's steps: "Tap the alert. Tap Continue and then tap Play Sound." "If you can't find the device and if you feel your safety is at risk, go to a safe public location and contact law enforcement." To disable it, "tap Instructions to Disable and follow the onscreen steps." The twist: "Disabling the Find My network on your device, turning off Bluetooth, or turning off Location Services on your iPhone does not prevent the owner of the AirTag, AirPods, or Find My network accessory from being able to see the location of that AirTag or accessory. You must disable the item by following the instructions above."

Google's steps: "Tap Play sound, which causes the tracker to make a sound." "After you find the tracker, you can: Go to a safe public location and contact law enforcement or a trusted contact if you feel that your safety is at risk. Get and save the tracker's info. Turn off the tracker." Google's twist: "If you turn off Bluetooth or location services, or turn on Airplane Mode, your phone won't prevent the owner of the tracker or device from finding the location of the tracker." And: "keep it turned on if you're concerned that turning it off could be unsafe."

Check yours. iPhone: "Go to Settings, tap Notifications, then tap Tracking Notifications. Turn on Allow Notifications." Apple also needs iOS 17.5 or later, Bluetooth and Location Services on, and Airplane Mode off. Android 12 and up: Settings › Safety & emergency › Unknown tracker alerts › Allow alerts; Scan now takes "about 10 seconds".

Apple Newsroom, May 13, 2024: Apple and Google made one industry specification so these alerts work "across both iOS and Android", in iOS 17.5 and on "Android 6.0+ devices."

Fine print: The alerts cover compatible trackers seen moving with you over time; they don't detect every kind of tracking. "You won't notify the owner if you play the sound" is Google's statement only. Google warns some trackers "may be factory reset" when turned off, and the owner "may still be able to check the last location". Android 11 and lower: Settings › Google › Personal & device safety. Apple: "Using these products to track people without their consent is a crime in many countries and regions around the world." In the US, both point to the Safety Net Project. The iPhone alert, Play Sound and Instructions to Disable screens and the Tracking Notifications menu are re-created by hand from Apple's wording; the Android alert and the Unknown tracker alerts menu are re-created by hand from Google's wording; the Bluetooth switch, the contact card and the phones are generic. The tag is a plain paper disc; no real interface or logo is shown. Not affiliated with Apple or Google.
